title.en: Physical action, pause and reset validation

summary: Validate a visible causal action against the declared model and restore its full initial state.
objective: Pause stops simulation time and motion; reset restores poses, velocities, input values, histories and pending time accumulation.
example_prompts: Validate a visible causal action against the declared model and restore its full initial state.

principles: Separate verification of equations or solver configuration from observation of the rendered interaction.
Choose a small representative scenario with a clear failure signal rather than testing every possible parameter.
implementation: Write initial state, action, expected outcome, tolerance and model limits before running. Include the camera view needed to see contact or constrained motion.
Run one release or impulse, pause mid-action, single-step if supported and reset. Inspect model state as well as the rendered result.
For a kinematic obstacle case, verify the authored query/controller prevents penetration or disclose that obstacle avoidance is outside scope.
Record passed, failed, skipped or not-run for each observation; a data validator cannot stand in for this runtime check.
observable_checks: Pause stops simulation time and motion; reset restores poses, velocities, input values, histories and pending time accumulation.
The named action visibly responds to its input and the observed result stays inside the stated model limits.

known_limits: This profile is not a promise of stable arbitrary configurations or a full dynamics certification.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt proportions, finish and presentation to the scene; explain deliberate departures from this guidance.

claims.statement: Kinematic Rapier bodies follow prescribed motion and ignore contact forces; avoiding obstacles requires additional handling.
claims.scope: A reason to check the application boundary, not proof that a particular scene handles it.
